3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: The primary endpoint (OS) was met with HR 0.675 (95% CI 0.568–0.801), p=0.0001. Median OS was not reached in the darolutamide arm vs 48.9 months in the placebo arm. Multiple secondary endpoints also succeeded: time to CRPC, pain progression, SSE-FS, time to first SSE, time to subsequent antineoplastic therapy, and time to opioid use. No formal subgroup analyses showing differential response by biomarker are reported in the extraction. The overall population responded strongly. The one failed secondary endpoint (physical symptoms) may reflect that symptom burden is influenced by docetaxel toxicity in both arms, masking a darolutamide benefit.

Safety profile was manageable — febrile neutropenia rates were nearly identical between arms (6.1% vs 6.0%), and the overall SAE pattern does not suggest dose-limiting toxicity prevented adequate dosing. Dose modifications were more frequent in the darolutamide arm (172 vs 112) but did not prevent the primary endpoint from being met. No high placebo response, no manufacturing issues, no commercial termination. The trial ran its full course.
